page: Amazon Web Services i4i.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is driven by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The CPU subsystem incorporates 54 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector and cryptographic extensions, including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 256 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a generous 8 GB per vCPU ratio.

Local direct-attached storage is a core architectural feature of the i4i.8xlarge, bundling 7,500 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 19 Gbps, supporting stable data throughput across distributed nodes without requiring shared storage mounts.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across synthetic compute and system evaluations. PassMark CPU reached 36,608.74 points, with Geekbench yielding a single-core score of 1,567 and a multi-core score of 13,416. Memory bandwidth for uncached read-only blocks measured 125.36 GB/sec, while uncached write operations achieved 62.92 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, Redis SET throughput maintained 31.16 million operations per second, PassMark database operations scored 14,843.76, and static web serving reached 35.05 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the i4i.8xlarge is the absence of discrete GPU acceleration, limiting execution speed on oversized artificial intelligence models. While small 135M parameter LLM text generation achieved 301.68 tokens per second, large 70B model prompt processing dropped to 6.2 tokens per second. Resource density makes this instance cost-effective for operational footprints requiring high NVMe capacity and memory density per socket without paying for accelerator overhead. The platform is best fitted for transactional relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, in-memory caches, search indexes, and high-frequency data pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.8xlarge is a storage-optimized cloud instance designed for high-throughput, latency-sensitive data operations. Built on the AWS Nitro system, it features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor offering 32 dedicated vCPUs at 3.5 GHz, 54 MB of L3 cache, and 256 GB of DDR4 system memory. Its hardware profile is highlighted by 7,500 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 19 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate balanced compute and memory throughput, scoring 36,608.74 on PassMark CPU and processing 31.16 million Redis SET operations per second. While lacking hardware accelerators for large-scale deep learning models, its high storage density and 8 GB per vCPU allocation make it an efficient deployment for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search engines, and real-time analytics platforms.
